items.q: Is the feedback produced by artificial intelligence?
a: No. The checks are rules written by RCF English. They look for things a computer can find reliably: whether a thesis states a position, whether a paragraph has an example, whether words are repeated, whether a conclusion adds new ideas, and so on.
They cannot judge how good your ideas are or correct every grammar mistake. Always compare your writing with the model, and ask a teacher to mark your finished essay.

items.q: Is my work saved?

pages.description: Speak your answers to IELTS Speaking Part 1, 2 and 3 questions, read sentences aloud and handle everyday situations. Your browser turns your speech into text and the page gives feedback on length, speed, pauses, reasons, examples, linking phrases and vocabulary.

hero.text: Hear the question, speak your answer, and see what you said. The page checks the things a computer can hear in your words: how long and how fast you spoke, whether you gave reasons and examples, and how varied your vocabulary was.

blocks.heading: Speak and check
blocks.noscript: Speaking practice needs JavaScript. You can still read the guides to [IELTS Speaking](practical-english/ielts/speaking/) and [Spoken English](practical-english/spoken-english/).

blocks.title: Getting the best results
bullets: Use **Chrome** or **Edge** on a computer or Android phone, or **Safari** on an iPhone or iPad. Firefox does not recognise speech; you can still use the timer and type your answer.
Find a quiet place and hold the phone about a hand-width from your mouth.
If the computer often mishears you, choose **English (India)** in the list. It is often better with Sri Lankan accents.
Speech recognition makes mistakes, especially with names. Correct the transcript, then press **Check again**.
Speak to the examiner, not the screen: answer, give a reason, add a detail.

items.q: Does it give me an IELTS band score?
a: No. A band score depends on grammar, pronunciation and how well ideas are developed, judged by a trained examiner. A computer counting words cannot do that honestly, so this page does not pretend to. It gives practice guidance you can act on.

items.q: What does it check?
a: **All speaking tasks:** the number of words, speaking time and speed, long pauses, reasons (*because*, *so*), linking phrases, repeated words, over-used words such as *good* and *very*, and fillers.
**Part 2:** whether your words suggest you covered the four points on the cue card.
**Part 3:** whether you gave an example, looked at the other side, and used future language for questions about the future.
**Read aloud:** which words of the sentence were recognised. A missed word may be a sound to practise, or the computer may simply have misheard.
**Everyday situations:** whether you used the language the situation needs, such as an apology, a polite request or thanks.

items.q: Can it check my pronunciation?
a: Only roughly. If a word is not recognised when you read a sentence aloud, it is worth listening to that word and trying again. But speech recognition is built to guess what you meant, so it often accepts a word even when the sound was not quite right, and it cannot hear word stress or intonation. A teacher is still the best judge of pronunciation.

items.q: Where does my voice go?
a: The speech recognition belongs to your browser, not to RCF English. **Chrome and Edge send the sound to Google, and Safari sends it to Apple**, to turn it into text. RCF English never receives your voice or your words. A short summary of each attempt (the date, the question, the number of words) is kept in your own browser so you can see your progress, and you can clear it at any time. See the [privacy policy](privacy/).

items.q: Are these real IELTS questions?
a: No. They are original questions written by RCF English in the style of the IELTS Speaking test. They are not official IELTS material and are not endorsed by the British Council, IDP: IELTS Australia or Cambridge University Press & Assessment.

hero.text: Eleven to fourteen minutes with an examiner who asks, listens and moves on, just like the real test. Choose from sixteen tests, each with different topics. Speak your answers; the examiner follows up if an answer is too short. At the end you get a transcript of the whole test and guidance on every answer.

blocks.title: Unofficial practice
text: An original RCF English practice test in the format of the IELTS Speaking test. The questions are not official IELTS material, and the test is not endorsed by the British Council, IDP: IELTS Australia or Cambridge University Press & Assessment. **It does not give a band score.**

blocks.heading: Your speaking test
blocks.noscript: The mock speaking test needs JavaScript and a browser that can recognise speech. You can still read the guide to [IELTS Speaking](practical-english/ielts/speaking/).

items.title: Part 1: introduction and interview (4 to 5 minutes)
text: The examiner asks your name, then questions on two familiar topics. If an answer is very short, you will hear a follow-up such as *Why?*

items.title: Part 2: the long turn (3 to 4 minutes)
text: The cue card appears on the screen and is read aloud. You have one minute to prepare. When the examiner asks you to begin, speak for up to two minutes; you will be stopped when the time is up.

items.title: Part 3: discussion (4 to 5 minutes)
text: More general questions linked to the Part 2 topic. Give opinions, reasons and examples, and look at both sides.

items.title: Your report
text: A transcript of every answer, how long and how fast you spoke, how often the examiner had to follow up, and practice guidance for each answer. You can print it for your teacher.

blocks.title: For the best results
bullets: Use **Chrome** or **Edge** on a computer or Android phone, or **Safari** on an iPhone or iPad.
Wear headphones if you can, and sit somewhere quiet.
The examiner moves on after you stop speaking for a few seconds. To move on sooner, press **I've finished my answer**.
If the microphone does not start by itself on your phone, an **Answer** button appears. Press it to speak.
Speech recognition is not perfect, especially with names and accents. If it often mishears you, choose **English (India)**.

items.q: Is the examiner a real person or an AI?
a: Neither. The examiner follows a fixed script, as real IELTS examiners do in Parts 1 and 2. The website listens for when you stop and for how much you said, which decides whether to ask a follow-up. It does not understand your ideas.

items.q: Why is there no band score?
a: A band depends on fluency and coherence, vocabulary, grammar and pronunciation, judged by a trained examiner. A computer counting words cannot do that honestly. The report shows what can be measured, so you know what to practise.

items.q: Where does my voice go?
a: Speech recognition is done by your browser. **Chrome and Edge send the audio to Google, and Safari sends it to Apple.** RCF English never receives your voice or your answers. See the [privacy policy](privacy/).

blocks.title: How to practise
bullets: Open **Useful phrases** before you start, and read them aloud once.
Speak in full sentences, and be polite: *Could I...*, *I'd like...*, *please* and *thank you*.
If you get stuck, press **Show an example**.
When you can do a conversation easily, switch off **Show what to say at each turn** and try again.
Use **Chrome**, **Edge** or **Safari**. In other browsers you can type your replies instead.

items.q: Does the website understand everything I say?
a: No. Each conversation is a script written by RCF English that branches on the words you use: for example, if you ask for coffee, the barista gives you coffee. It covers the replies a learner is likely to give, but it does not understand free conversation and it does not correct your grammar.

items.q: Can I practise playing a part in a written conversation?
a: Yes. On the [Spoken English](practical-english/spoken-english/) page, each conversation has **Take a part and speak it** buttons: the website speaks the other person's lines and listens for yours.

items.q: Where does my voice go?
a: Speech recognition is done by your browser. **Chrome and Edge send the audio to Google, and Safari sends it to Apple.** RCF English never receives your voice or your words. See the [privacy policy](privacy/).

Answer before you look. Guessing and then reading the explanation teaches more than reading alone.
Read every explanation, including the ones for answers you got right.
Do the activity a second time a few days later. That is when it settles.

items.q: Do I need to create an account?
a: No. Nothing on RCF English requires an account, a login or a password. The interactive activities run inside your own browser.

items.q: Does the site work on a telephone?
a: Yes. Every page is designed for small screens first, including the timetable, which appears as cards rather than a wide table on a telephone.

items.q: Will it work on a slow connection?
a: It should. The pages are plain files with no heavy libraries, no video and no advertising scripts, so they load quickly even on a weak signal.

items.q: Can I print a lesson?
a: Yes. Use your browser's print command. The menus, buttons and footer are removed automatically so that only the lesson is printed.

items.q: Is everything free?
a: Everything on RCF English is free to read and use. Books and study guides are sold separately through RCF Publications, which is a different website.

pages.title: Frequently Asked Questions
pages.description: Answers to common questions about RCF English: what it covers, who it is for, past papers and copyright, interactive activities, RCF Online Academy and RCF Publications.

hero.text: If your question is not answered here, please [contact us](contact/) and ask.

items.q: What is RCF English?
a: RCF English is an educational platform that brings together English-language learning, literature education, examination support, teacher resources, online classes and links to educational publications in one place.

items.q: Who is it for?
a: School students, O/L and A/L learners, adult English learners, private candidates, schoolteachers, tuition teachers and parents. Particular attention is given to learners who need additional guidance, including those in rural and remote areas.

items.q: Who runs it?
a: RCF English was founded by Rohana Fernando, an experienced English teacher and lecturer. His qualifications and background are set out on the [Academic and Professional Background](about/background/) page.

items.q: Does it cost anything?
a: No. Everything on this website is free to read and use. Books and study guides are sold separately through RCF Publications, which is a different website with its own ordering arrangements.

items.q: Is RCF English connected to any government body?
a: No. RCF English is an independent educational platform. It is not endorsed by, approved by or affiliated with any government department or examination authority, and it makes no claim to be.

items.q: Which subjects are covered?
a: O/L English, O/L English Literature, General English and A/L English Literature, together with past papers, teacher resources and interactive practice.

items.q: Why can I not find a past paper I am looking for?
a: Because RCF English publishes only what it is entitled to publish. A paper appears here if RCF English created it, if the copyright holder has permitted its distribution, if it has been personally approved, or if it can lawfully be linked from the official source. Papers that do not meet one of these tests are not published, even if copies of them exist elsewhere.

items.q: Are the model answers official answers?
a: No. Model answers on this site are written by RCF English to show how an answer can be built and why it works. They are teaching material, not official marking scheme answers, and they are not the only acceptable answers.

items.q: Can I use this material in my classroom?
a: Yes, for teaching. Material created by RCF English may be used and printed for classroom and study purposes with acknowledgement. Please do not republish it as your own or sell it. See the [Terms of Use](terms/).

items.q: Are complete poems, stories and plays reproduced here?
a: No. Copyrighted literary texts are not reproduced in full. RCF English provides summaries, analysis, themes, character notes, questions and model answers, with short quotations where they are needed for study and criticism.

items.q: Do the activities record my answers?
a: No. The activities run entirely inside your browser. Nothing is sent anywhere, nothing is saved once you close the page, and no personal information is collected.

items.q: Do they work on a telephone?
a: Yes. All the activities are designed for touch as well as for a mouse and a keyboard, including the sentence-ordering activity, which uses buttons rather than dragging.

items.q: Can I do an activity more than once?
a: Yes. Every activity has a Start again button, and repeating an activity a few days later is one of the most useful things you can do.

items.q: How do I join a class?
a: Choose a class, contact RCF Online Academy on WhatsApp, and you will be sent the schedule, fee and availability information. Registration is confirmed by the teacher; it is not automatic.

items.q: Why are the days, times and fees not shown on the website?
a: Because they change, and publishing an out-of-date schedule helps nobody. Where a detail has not been settled, the site says so honestly. Ask on WhatsApp and you will be told what currently applies.

items.q: Are the classes online or in a classroom?
a: Classes are conducted mainly online, which allows students in any part of the country to attend.

items.q: What do I need in order to attend?
a: A device with an internet connection, a notebook and a pen. Spoken English classes also need a working microphone.

items.q: What is RCF Publications?
a: RCF Publications is the publishing and bookshop division associated with RCF English. It produces practical educational books, English support materials, literature study guides, grammar resources and examination-revision materials.

items.q: Is it part of this website?
a: Yes. RCF Publications is a section of this website, kept separate from the free material so that paid and free resources are never confused.

items.q: How do I buy a book?
a: Choose the title, then follow the payment instructions on the page. Payment is by bank transfer, and you send the receipt through WhatsApp. No payment is processed on this website and no card details are ever requested.

pages.title: Copyright and Resource Policy
pages.description: How RCF English decides what may be published, how copyrighted material is treated, and how to request the removal of anything published in error.
pages.keywords: copyright policy, resource policy, permission, takedown

hero.text: This page sets out, plainly, what RCF English will and will not publish. It applies to every past paper, worksheet, model answer and literary extract on the site.

blocks.title: Reporting a copyright concern
text: RCF English respects intellectual-property rights. If you are a copyright owner and believe that any material available through this website has been used improperly, please [contact us](contact/) with the resource title and evidence of ownership. We will investigate and, where appropriate, remove or correct the material promptly.

This notice is how an owner reaches us. It is **not** permission to publish copyrighted material, and we do not treat it as one: a resource is checked for ownership and redistribution permission **before** it goes on the site, not after a complaint arrives.

blocks.heading: How a resource is classified before it is published
text: Every file offered here falls into one of these groups, and only the first three are ever published:
**1. Written by RCF English.** Our own lessons, notes and practice material.
**2. Official Sri Lankan government material clearly released for public access.** Where an official page or download exists we **link to it** rather than host a second copy.
**3. Third-party material with explicit permission to redistribute.**

Everything else is held back: commercial books, scans of books, copyrighted workbooks, files with no stated author, and material made by other teachers or institutions without permission. **Crediting an author or an education office is not permission.** Anything uncertain is marked *Copyright and permission review required* and stays unpublished until ownership is confirmed.

Our own books are a separate case. Books published by RCF Publications are sold through their retailer and may be enrolled in schemes that require the digital edition to remain exclusive to that shop. We therefore show the cover, the description and a link to buy, and we do **not** place the complete book on this site, even while it is on a free promotion.

blocks.heading: The rule we work by
text: A resource is published on RCF English only if **at least one** of the following is true.
The existence of a copy of a document — in a shared folder, on a messaging group, or anywhere else on the internet — is **not** permission to publish it.
numbered: RCF English created the resource itself.
The copyright holder has given permission for it to be distributed.
Rohana Fernando has personally approved its publication.
It can lawfully be linked — not copied — from the official website that publishes it.

blocks.heading: In practice
do: Lessons, explanations and guidance written by RCF English
Model questions and model answers written by RCF English
Worksheets and revision material created by RCF English
Papers whose copyright holder has given permission
Links to past papers on the official websites that publish them
Short quotations from literary works, for study and criticism, with the author named
dont: Copyrighted past papers copied without permission
Complete copyrighted poems, stories, plays or novels
Complete paid eBooks or books belonging to any publisher
Marking schemes we are not entitled to distribute
Anyone's private files, correspondence or personal data
Material of uncertain origin, on the assumption that it is probably fine

blocks.heading: Literary texts
text: Literature teaching needs the text, but copyright law protects it. RCF English handles this in the following way.
Where a text is out of copyright, longer extracts may be given. Where a text is still in copyright, the study material stands on its own and the student is expected to have the prescribed book.
bullets: Summaries, plot outlines, character notes, themes and analysis are original work written by RCF English and are published freely.
Context questions, essay questions, model answers and revision exercises are written by RCF English.
Quotations are kept short, are used for study and criticism, and always name the author and the work.
Complete copyrighted texts are never reproduced.

blocks.heading: Material created by RCF English
text: Lessons, guidance, model answers, worksheets and activities on this site were written by RCF English unless a different author is named on the page.

Teachers and students may use and print this material for teaching, learning and revision, with acknowledgement. It may not be republished as someone else's work, sold, or included in a commercial product without written permission. Books published by RCF Publications are sold separately and are not covered by this permission.

blocks.title: If you believe something here should not be
text: If you are a copyright owner, or you act for one, and you believe material on this site has been published without the right to do so, please tell us. Material that is the subject of a genuine complaint is taken down while the position is checked — it is not left up while the matter is argued.
Use the [Corrections and Takedown Requests](corrections/) page, which sets out exactly what to include so that the request can be dealt with quickly.

blocks.heading: No official status is claimed
text: RCF English is an independent educational platform. It is not endorsed by, approved by, or affiliated with any government department, examination authority or public institution, and nothing on this site should be read as suggesting otherwise.
Model answers and guidance on this site are teaching material prepared by RCF English. They are not official answers, and no guarantee of any examination result is made or implied.

pages.title: Corrections and Takedown Requests

hero.text: Mistakes happen. A correction sent today improves the material for everyone who uses it tomorrow, so please do send it.

items.title: A broken link or a technical fault
text: A link that leads nowhere, a page that will not open, an activity that does not work, or a layout problem on your device.

items.title: A copyright concern

blocks.heading: Copyright complaints
text: If you own the copyright in material published on this site, or you act for the owner, and you believe it has been published without permission, please send the following. With these details a request can be dealt with quickly; without them it may be delayed while the material is identified.

pages.title: Privacy Policy
pages.description: What RCF English does and does not collect: no accounts and no advertising; how visits are counted; what your own browser keeps on your device; and how details you give when buying from RCF Publications are used.

hero.text: Effective date: 14 September 2026. The short version: this website does not collect anything about you while you read and practise. Some choices are kept on your own device, and details you choose to send when buying are used only for that purchase. The longer version is below.

blocks.heading: What this website collects
text: **Nothing is sent to RCF English while you use the site.** RCF English is a set of ordinary files served to your browser. It has no accounts, no login, no database and no server-side program that could record a visit.

In particular, this website does not use analytics or tracking scripts, does not use behavioural advertising, does not set advertising cookies or cookies of its own, does not ask for your name, email address or telephone number in order to read anything, and does not build a profile of you.

Some features remember your choices by saving them **in your own browser, on your own device**. That is explained under *What is kept on your device* below. The site also carries paid educational listings and sells books and resource collections; both are explained in their own sections.

blocks.heading: What this website collects
text: **RCF English does not know who you are.** RCF English is a set of ordinary files served to your browser. It has no accounts, no login and no database of visitors.

This website does not use behavioural advertising, does not set advertising cookies or cookies of its own, does not ask for your name, email address or telephone number in order to read anything, and does not build a profile of you. It does count visits anonymously, as explained under *Visitor statistics* below.

Some features remember your choices by saving them **in your own browser, on your own device**. That is explained under *What is kept on your device* below. The site also carries paid educational listings and sells books and resource collections; both are explained in their own sections.

blocks.heading: What this website collects
text: **RCF English does not know who you are.** RCF English is a set of ordinary files served to your browser. It has no accounts, no login and no database of visitors.

This website does not use behavioural advertising, does not show adverts from an advertising network, does not ask for your name, email address or telephone number in order to read anything, and does not build a profile of you. It does use **Google Analytics** to count visits, which sets cookies in your browser, as explained under *Visitor statistics* below.

Some features remember your choices by saving them **in your own browser, on your own device**. That is explained under *What is kept on your device* below. The site also carries paid educational listings and sells books and resource collections; both are explained in their own sections.

blocks.heading: Visitor statistics
text: To find out which lessons and resources are used, and which need improving, this site counts page visits with **[[analytics-service]]**, a statistics service that does not use cookies.
**What is counted:** the page you viewed, the website that sent you (if any), the general type of device and browser, the approximate country, and how quickly the page loaded.

**What is not collected:** no cookies are set and nothing is stored on your device for statistics. RCF English sees only totals, such as how many times a page was viewed. It never sees your IP address, your name or anything else that identifies you, and the statistics are not used to follow you across other websites or for advertising.
If your browser or a content blocker stops the statistics script, nothing changes: every page works exactly the same.

blocks.heading: Visitor statistics
text: To find out which lessons and resources are used, and which need improving, this site uses **Google Analytics**, a statistics service provided by Google.

**What it collects:** the pages you view and how long you stay, the website or search that brought you here, the general type of device, browser and screen, your approximate location (such as country and city), and a random identifier so that return visits can be counted. Google receives your IP address in order to work out the approximate location; Google Analytics 4 does not log or store IP addresses.
**Cookies:** Google Analytics stores cookies whose names begin with *_ga* in your browser. They do not contain your name or contact details. Unless you clear them, they last for up to two years.

**What RCF English sees:** reports of totals, such as how many people viewed a page or which countries visitors came from. RCF English cannot identify you from these reports, does not combine them with any other information about you, and does not use them for advertising.
Google's own use of this information is explained on its page [How Google uses information from sites or apps that use its services](https://policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites).

**If you prefer not to be counted:** block or delete cookies in your browser settings, use a content blocker, or install Google's [Analytics opt-out browser add-on](https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout). Every page works exactly the same without it.

blocks.heading: Sponsored listings
text: Tuition classes and courses run by other people can be advertised on this site as paid listings. Every one of them is clearly marked **Sponsored**, and paid listings are kept in their own section, never mixed into the free lessons or resources.

These listings are plain text and pictures written into the site. They are not served by an advertising network. Nothing about you is sent to an advertiser, no advertising cookie is set, and what you see does not change according to who you are or what you have looked at before.
RCF English does not endorse an advertiser by accepting a listing. Anything you arrange with one is between you and them.

blocks.heading: Buying books, resources and advertising
text: Books, resource collections, advertising and class fees are at present paid for by bank transfer, arranged directly with RCF. The site shows you the account details and what to write on the transfer; your bank handles the payment, not this website.

**No payment is processed on this website at present.** There is no checkout, no payment gateway and no card processing. You will never be asked on this site for a card number, an online-banking password, a PIN, a one-time code or an identity-document number, and you should never enter one anywhere on it.

Because a static website cannot verify a deposit, every payment is checked by a person. You send the receipt through WhatsApp, and what you send in that message reaches RCF through WhatsApp rather than through this site.

parts.heading: Information you give when you buy
text: To confirm a payment and deliver a product, RCF Publications needs a few details from you, such as your name, the WhatsApp number or email address the product should be sent to, and your payment receipt or reference.

These details are used only to confirm your payment, deliver what you bought, answer questions about the purchase and handle any request under the [Refund and Return Policy](rcf-publications/refund-policy/). They are not sold, and they are not shared with anyone except where needed to complete the purchase, such as your bank or a payment provider.

parts.heading: Online payment providers
text: If online payment through a provider such as PayHere is introduced, your card or account details will be entered on the provider's own secure payment page and processed by that provider under its own privacy terms. RCF Publications will not see or store your card details. This policy will be updated before any such payment method is made available.
Purchases are also covered by the [Terms and Conditions](rcf-publications/terms/) of RCF Publications.

blocks.heading: Interactive activities and tools
text: The quizzes, listening tests, writing practice, worksheet generator, flashcard maker, study timetable and examination timer run entirely inside your own browser. What you type and how you answer are not transmitted anywhere, and visitor statistics do not record your answers. The one exception is speech recognition on the Speaking Practice page, explained below. No one, including RCF English, can see your answers.
Some of these tools keep your progress or your work on your device so that it is there when you come back, as described in the next section.

blocks.heading: Speaking practice and speech recognition
text: The [Speaking Practice](speaking-practice/), [IELTS Mock Speaking Test](practical-english/ielts/mock-speaking-test/) and [Conversation Partner](practical-english/conversation-partner/) pages, and the role-play buttons on spoken English conversations, use your browser's own speech recognition to turn what you say into text. **Your voice goes to your browser's maker, not to RCF English.**

When you press Start speaking, your browser asks for permission to use the microphone. While you speak, **Chrome and Microsoft Edge send the sound of your voice to Google, and Safari sends it to Apple**, which send back the words. Their own privacy policies apply to that. RCF English never receives your voice, a recording or the words.

The page explains this and asks you to confirm before you use it for the first time. It keeps a short summary of your recent attempts (the date, the question, the number of words and the speaking speed) in your own browser so you can see your progress, and you can clear it on the page at any time. This site keeps no recording of your voice anywhere.
Nothing is heard unless you press Start speaking, and recognition stops when you press Stop, when the time limit is reached or when you leave the page.

blocks.heading: What is kept on your device
text: To remember your choices without an account, the site saves a small amount of information in your browser's own storage (known as local storage). **It stays on the device you are using. It is not sent to RCF English or to anyone else, and it is not shared with your other devices.** It can include:

bullets: the grade you chose on **My RCF English**, the pages you saved, and the pages you viewed recently
your stars and best scores in the interactive activities, and your chosen support level
drafts in **Writing Practice**, words typed into the flashcard maker, and your study timetable
an examination date you entered for the countdown
your reading options (text size, high contrast, spacing) and your preferred listening accent and sound settings

parts.heading: Offline copies
text: So that pages you have already opened can be read without a connection, your browser also keeps copies of those pages and of the site's style and script files. These are ordinary website files, not information about you, and they are replaced automatically when the site is updated.

parts.heading: Removing it
text: You can remove everything the site has saved with the **Clear everything saved on this device** button on [My RCF English](my/), or by clearing this website's data in your browser settings. Using a private or incognito window means nothing is kept after you close it.

blocks.heading: Forms, WhatsApp and email
text: Because there is no server behind this website, the contact forms cannot send anything. What they do instead is write your message for you and hand it to WhatsApp or to your own email program, where **you** press send.

That means the message travels through WhatsApp or through your email provider, and their own privacy terms apply to it, not ours. Please do not include information in such a message that you would not want to share.
Any message you do send is used only to answer you.

blocks.heading: Hosting and links to other websites
text: This website is published through GitHub Pages. Like any web host, GitHub processes the requests your browser makes in order to deliver the pages, and its own terms govern that processing. RCF English does not receive or keep any of it.

RCF English links to other websites — chiefly official examination sources, where a paper is linked rather than copied. Once you follow such a link you are on a different website, with its own privacy practices. Links that leave this site are marked, and open in a new tab. Some official Sri Lankan government sites are served over plain HTTP rather than HTTPS; where that is so, the link is marked. RCF Publications is not an external link: it is a section of this website.

blocks.heading: Children
text: Much of this material is intended for school students. Since nothing is collected from anybody while they use the site, nothing is collected from children either. No account can be created, and no personal detail is requested anywhere on the site. Progress and choices a child makes are kept only on the device they are using. Purchases and class registrations are arranged by an adult through WhatsApp and a bank transfer, away from this website.

blocks.heading: Changes and questions
text: If this policy changes, the new version replaces this page and the effective date at the top is updated.

If you have a question about privacy, or would like details you sent when buying, or a message you sent us, to be deleted, please contact us through the [Contact](contact/) page, by email at [rcfdegreenotes@gmail.com](mailto:rcfdegreenotes@gmail.com), or on WhatsApp at [070 439 5240](https://wa.me/94704395240).

pages.title: Terms of Use
pages.description: The terms on which RCF English material may be used, what is guaranteed and what is not, and how the site relates to RCF Online Academy and RCF Publications.

hero.text: Plain terms for a free educational website. By using RCF English you accept them.

blocks.heading: Using the material
text: Everything on RCF English is free to read. Material created by RCF English may be used, printed and shared for teaching, learning and revision, provided that RCF English is acknowledged as the source.

You may not republish RCF English material as your own work, sell it, or include it in a product or service that is sold, without written permission. Books published by RCF Publications are sold separately and are not covered by this permission.

blocks.heading: Accuracy
text: This material is prepared carefully, but no website is free of error, and syllabuses, examination formats and prescribed texts change from time to time.

**Always check the current official syllabus and examination instructions for your own examination year.** Where this site describes an examination, it is describing it as a teacher would; it is not an official statement of the examination requirements.
If you find a mistake, please [tell us](corrections/) so that it can be put right.

blocks.title: No guarantee of results, and no official status
text: RCF English does not promise, and cannot promise, any particular examination result. Results depend on the student's own work.
RCF English is an independent platform. It is not endorsed by, approved by or affiliated with any government department, examination authority or public institution.

blocks.heading: Model answers
text: Model answers on this site are teaching material written by RCF English to show how an answer can be built and why it works. They are not official answers, they are not the only acceptable answers, and they should not be memorised and reproduced. Copying a model answer into an examination script is not a route to a good mark.

blocks.heading: RCF Online Academy
text: Class information on this site is descriptive. Nothing on this website constitutes an offer of a place, and no registration is completed on this website. A place is confirmed only by RCF Online Academy directly, after contact on WhatsApp.
Where a schedule, fee or number of places has not been settled, the site says so rather than guessing.

blocks.heading: RCF Publications and other websites
text: RCF Publications is a separate section of this website with its own ordering arrangements. Books, resource collections and advertising are paid for by bank transfer arranged directly with RCF and verified by a person. No payment is processed on this website, no card details are requested, and nothing is charged automatically.
RCF English is not responsible for the content of any other website it links to, including official sources for past papers.

blocks.heading: Availability
text: This site is provided as it is, without a guarantee that it will always be available or free of fault. It is offered as an educational service, without charge.

pages.title: Accessibility Statement
pages.description: How RCF English is built to be usable with a keyboard, a screen reader, magnification and a small screen, what has been tested, and how to report a barrier.
pages.keywords: accessibility statement, WCAG, screen reader, keyboard navigation

hero.text: This site is built so that it can be used by people who navigate with a keyboard, who use a screen reader, who need large text, or who are on a small or old device.

blocks.heading: What we aim for
text: RCF English aims to follow the **Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, level AA** as a standard of good practice. This is a statement of intent and of the work actually done; it is not a certificate, and no formal audit has been carried out.

blocks.heading: What has been built in
bullets: **Semantic HTML** — real headings, lists, tables and landmarks, so assistive technology can describe the page.
**A skip-to-content link** at the top of every page, so keyboard users can pass the menu.

**Full keyboard operation** — every menu, activity and form can be used without a mouse. Menus open with Enter or Space and with the Down arrow, close with Escape, and return focus to the button that opened them.
**A visible focus outline** on every interactive element. It is never removed.
**Colour contrast** that meets the AA ratio for body text, headings and interface text.
**No information carried by colour alone.** A right or wrong answer is shown by a word as well as by a colour.
**Labels on every form field**, and errors described in words beside the field they belong to.
**Reduced-motion support** — if your system asks for less motion, animation and smooth scrolling are switched off.
**Large touch targets** — buttons and links are at least 44 pixels high.
**Alternative text** on images that carry meaning; decorative graphics are hidden from screen readers.
**Tables that become cards** on narrow screens, so the class timetable is readable on a telephone.
**No horizontal scrolling** at any screen width from 320 pixels upwards.

blocks.heading: What has actually been tested
text: Being honest about this matters more than a long list. The following has been checked directly:
bullets: Keyboard operation of the menus, the mobile drawer, the search page, the filters and all ten interactive activities.
Layout at 320, 375, 768, 1024 and large desktop widths, with no horizontal scrolling.
Heading order on every page.
Colour contrast of the text and interface colours against their backgrounds.
That every internal link on the site points at a page that exists — this is checked automatically every time the site is rebuilt.

blocks.title: Known limitations
bullets: The interactive activities need JavaScript. Where JavaScript is unavailable, a message explains this and points to the written lessons instead.
Search and the resource filters also need JavaScript. Without it, the menus and the [How to Use This Site](how-to-use/) page list every section.
The site has not been tested with every combination of screen reader and browser. If you meet a barrier, please tell us — that is more useful than any claim on this page.
